result:
The proposed answer of 2/3 looks wrong. It is also unsupported: the solution only asserts symmetry and never computes anything.

A line through two interior points meets the hexagon's boundary in exactly two points, so the question is whether those two boundary points lie on opposite edges.

A direction parallel to a pair of edges shows the probability is not as large as 2/3. A line parallel to the top and bottom edges crosses the two upper slanted edges, or the two lower ones. These are never opposite edges, so such lines contribute nothing. This direction is not special in the sense of being negligible, because the nearby directions behave similarly. This points to a value below 2/3.

I did not carry out the full integral. I am relying on my recollection of this problem (an HMMT problem), whose answer I believe is 4/9, not 2/3. This is a recalled value, not something I derived here.

VERDICT: REJECT
